entries.root_cause: Host-inventory completion fenced generation, configuration and scope authority but had no monotonic poll-order authority. Two operations claimed under the same source revision could therefore complete out of order, allowing an older provider snapshot to overwrite or remove state established by a newer snapshot.
horizontal_audit: host inventory claim and completion authority
future problem and topology snapshot ingestion

entries.root_cause: The negative-presence transition guard proved that a complete authoritative snapshot omitted a host, but it did not prove that the negative snapshot was newer than the resource's latest confirmed positive observation. Historical negative evidence could therefore be replayed to reverse a newer positive state.
horizontal_audit: future metric tombstone and deletion semantics
future reconciliation paths that consume historical evidence

entries.root_cause: The first poll-order remediation wrapped completion by renaming the previously unfenced implementation and delegating to it after checking poll authority. That left an alternate callable SQL entry point which a broadly granted runtime role could invoke directly, bypassing the newly introduced authority fence while preserving otherwise valid tenant context.
horizontal_audit: all SQL helper functions introduced by authority wrappers
runtime roles receiving broad function execute grants
completion and reconciliation alternate entry points
future internal helper extraction around fenced mutations
provider worker functions whose public surface must equal their authority surface
